title: The dog on the way back
description: A bushcraft club, a dog without a leash and a lot of tenses.
original: So one days I was with my kids. I leads kids club of buscraft skills, so I was with them. And we were on our way back from our hidden place and I noticed a dog. He was running directly ahead of us (oprav mi tohle, chci říct, že běžel přímo proti nám). I'm quite aware of dogs behaviour, so I knew I need to get its attention. So I called at it (můžu používat at him?) and started to play (nebo playing) with him shortly. He tried to sniff my kids also, but all of them was smaller than it or at least as tall as him. So I was still standing between them and him and after a while he lost his attention and run back to its owners. By that time I was really pissed! Before he run back to their owners I started yealling at them. I was super pissed because I was yealed something like "what does it mean?" and "you are not able to controll him" and "where is your leash?"... But they didn't respond at all. They kept quiet. So it made mi piss much more. So I started push them to say anything and they said only "don't panic, it can feel your anger and it can be more angry"....Long story short I made it easy and tell them that they know they need to control their dog and if anything is not clear we can call cops. I need to leave before I start to be furious:)

versions.en: {So one days|One day} I was with my kids. I {leads kids club of buscraft skills|lead a bushcraft club for kids}, so I was with them. {And we|We} were on our way back from our {hidden place and I noticed a dog|secret spot when I noticed a dog}. {He was running directly ahead of us|He was running straight towards us}. {I'm quite aware of dogs behaviour|I know a lot about dog behaviour}, so I knew I {need|needed} to get {its|his} attention. {So I called at it and started to play with him shortly|I called out to him and played with him for a short while}. {He tried to sniff my kids also, but all of them was smaller than it or at least as tall as him|He also tried to sniff my kids, but they were all smaller than him, or at most as tall as him}. {So I was still standing|I kept standing} between them and him{ and|, and} after a while he {lost his attention and run back to its owners|lost interest and ran back to his owners}. {By that time|At that point} I was really {pissed|pissed off}. {Before he run back to their owners I started yealling at them|After he ran back to his owners, I started yelling at them}. {I was super pissed because I was yealed something like "what does it mean?" and "you are not able to controll him" and "where is your leash?"...|I was super pissed off, so I yelled something like "What is this supposed to mean?", "You can't control him!" and "Where's your leash?"} But they didn't respond at all. They kept quiet. {So it made mi piss much more|That made me even more pissed off}. {So I started push them to say anything and they said only|So I started pushing them to say something, and they only said,} "Don't panic, {it can feel your anger and it can be more angry|he can sense your anger and get angrier}." {Long story short I made it easy and tell them that they know they need to control their dog and if anything is not clear we can call cops|Long story short, I kept it simple and told them that they had to control their dog and that if anything wasn't clear, we could call the cops}. {I need to leave before I start to be furious|I had to leave before I lost my temper}. :)
versions.cz: Jednoho dne jsem byl se svými dětmi. Vedu dětský bushcraftový kroužek, takže jsem byl s nimi. Vraceli jsme se z našeho tajného místa, když jsem si všiml psa. Běžel přímo proti nám. O chování psů toho dost vím, takže jsem věděl, že musím upoutat jeho pozornost. Zavolal jsem na něj a chvíli jsem si s ním hrál. Také se pokusil očichat moje děti, ale všechny byly menší než on, nebo nanejvýš stejně vysoké. Pořád jsem stál mezi nimi a ním a po chvíli ztratil zájem a utekl zpátky ke svým majitelům. V tu chvíli jsem byl opravdu naštvaný. Když utekl zpátky k majitelům, začal jsem na ně křičet. Byl jsem strašně naštvaný, tak jsem křičel něco jako „Co to má znamenat?“, „Nedokážete ho ovládat!“ a „Kde máte vodítko?“ Ale vůbec nereagovali. Mlčeli. To mě naštvalo ještě víc. Začal jsem na ně tlačit, ať něco řeknou, a oni jen řekli: „Nepanikařte, cítí váš hněv a může být ještě agresivnější.“ Zkrátka a dobře, nekomplikoval jsem to a řekl jsem jim, že musí svého psa ovládat a že pokud něco není jasné, můžeme zavolat policii. Musel jsem odejít dřív, než přijdu o nervy. :)

versions.en: You won't believe what [[has happened]]! I[['ve just got]] back from my bushcraft club with the kids, and we[['ve had]] a run-in with a dog without a leash. We were on our way back from our secret spot when I noticed him running straight towards us. I know a lot about dog behaviour, so I knew I needed to get his attention. I called out to him and played with him for a short while. He tried to sniff my kids too, but they were all smaller than him, so I kept standing between them and him. After a while he lost interest and ran back to his owners. I[['ve never been]] so angry at dog owners! I[['ve just yelled]] at them: "What is this supposed to mean? You can't control him! Where's your leash?" They [[haven't said]] a word. That [[has made]] me even more pissed off. I told them that they have to control their dog, and that if anything isn't clear, we can call the cops. I[['ve just walked]] away from them, because I didn't want to lose my temper.
versions.cz: Nebudeš věřit, co se stalo! Právě jsem se s dětmi vrátil z našeho bushcraftového kroužku a měli jsme potyčku se psem bez vodítka. Vraceli jsme se z našeho tajného místa, když jsem si všiml, jak běží přímo proti nám. O chování psů toho dost vím, takže jsem věděl, že musím upoutat jeho pozornost. Zavolal jsem na něj a chvíli jsem si s ním hrál. Chtěl očichat i moje děti, ale všechny byly menší než on, tak jsem pořád stál mezi nimi a ním. Po chvíli ztratil zájem a utekl zpátky ke svým majitelům. Nikdy jsem na majitele psů nebyl tak naštvaný! Právě jsem na ně křičel: „Co to má znamenat? Nedokážete ho ovládat! Kde máte vodítko?“ Neřekli ani slovo. To mě naštvalo ještě víc. Řekl jsem jim, že musí svého psa ovládat, a že pokud něco není jasné, můžeme zavolat policii. Právě jsem od nich odešel, protože jsem nechtěl přijít o nervy.

versions.en: I[['ve had]] a stressful week. Every afternoon I[['ve led]] my bushcraft club for kids, and nothing [[has gone]] wrong so far. Until today! Today a dog [[has run]] straight towards us on our way back from our secret spot. I know a lot about dog behaviour, so I[['ve called]] out to him and played with him for a short while. He [[has]] also [[tried]] to sniff my kids, but I[['ve kept]] standing between them and him. Finally he [[has lost]] interest and run back to his owners. I[['ve never been]] so angry at dog owners! I[['ve asked]] them, "Where's your leash?" and "Why can't you control him?", but they [[haven't said]] a word. That [[has made]] me even angrier. I[['ve just told]] them that they have to control their dog, and I[[ haven't calmed]] down yet.
versions.cz: Měl jsem stresující týden. Každé odpoledne jsem vedl svůj dětský bushcraftový kroužek a zatím se nic nepokazilo. Až dnes! Dnes na nás cestou zpátky z našeho tajného místa přiběhl pes. O chování psů toho dost vím, takže jsem na něj zavolal a chvíli jsem si s ním hrál. Také se pokusil očichat moje děti, ale já pořád stál mezi nimi a ním. Nakonec ztratil zájem a utekl zpátky ke svým majitelům. Nikdy jsem na majitele psů nebyl tak naštvaný! Zeptal jsem se jich: „Kde máte vodítko?“ a „Proč ho nedokážete ovládat?“, ale neřekli ani slovo. To mě naštvalo ještě víc. Právě jsem jim řekl, že musí svého psa ovládat, a pořád jsem se neuklidnil.

changes.heading: Tenses
items: I knew I need → I knew I needed: after a past tense (knew) the next verb moves into the past too.
he run back → he ran back: run is irregular (run, ran, run).
Before he run back, I started yelling → After he ran back, I started yelling: first he ran off, then you yelled.
I made it easy and tell them → I kept it simple and told them: both verbs must be in the past.
they know they need → they had to; wasn’t clear, we could: reported speech moves back in time.
before I start to be furious → before I lost my temper: “start to be” isn’t used; say get furious or lose my temper.
all of them was → all of them were; I leads → I lead: the -s belongs only to he/she/it.
I was yealed something → I yelled something: you don’t want the passive here.

changes.heading: Words and phrases
items: directly ahead of us means “in front of us, going the same way”. You wanted straight towards us.
call at it → call out to him. Yell at / shout at means shouting angrily at someone.
him / it / its / their: a dog can be he, she or it, but don’t mix them. Here it’s he, him, his.
started to play / started playing: both are correct.
shortly means “soon”. For “a little while” use briefly or for a short while.
also goes before the verb (He also tried…); at the end of a sentence use too.
at least as tall means “as tall or taller”, the opposite of what you meant. Use at most as tall or no taller than.
say anything → say something (anything is for negatives and questions).
